clue.text: Country pub's hosting bachelor party

indicators.note: a host takes guests in, so the pub's letters go round the others

blocks.note: a pub is a bar; the 's makes it plural here
BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A country pub is putting on someone's stag night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bachelor party' reads as a stag do, but the two words give separate pieces, a degree and a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbados is an island nation in the Caribbean, so it is a sovereign state.

clue.text: Open ChatGPT perhaps on track

blocks.note: ChatGPT is an example of artificial intelligence
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a track

explanation.surface: A question about whether the chatbot is open-source and doing well.
explanation.definitionFit: An airy room is spacious and exposed to fresh air, so it feels open.

clue.text: Artist relies on secrecy ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so only the closing letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: to bank on something is to rely on it
the final letter of secrecy

explanation.surface: An artist depends on staying anonymous.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is apt: BANKSY is the street artist famous for keeping his identity secret.
explanation.definitionFit: Banksy is the anonymous British graffiti and street artist, an example of a painter.

clue.text: Adolescent graffiti drawing in evening on ecstasy

indicators.note: drawing something in means pulling it inside, so one piece swallows the other

blocks.note: a tag is a graffiti artist's signature
e'en is a poetic contraction of evening
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A teenager spraying graffiti at night while high on drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: TAG opens to take in EEN, giving T-EEN-AG, then E goes underneath in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Teenage is an adjective describing someone aged thirteen to nineteen, the years of youth.

clue.text: White on the move with queen sacrificed

indicators.note: a piece sacrificed is given up and taken off the board, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: astir means up and moving about
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A chess move: White advances by giving up the queen.
explanation.walkthrough: ASTIR loses its R. The chess picture makes White look like the player, but it is a wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling white wine from Piedmont in northern Italy.

clue.text: He's nursing poor appetite

indicators.note: something poor is in bad shape, so these letters are knocked into a different order

blocks.note: the letters as written, ten of them

explanation.surface: A man looking after a patient who will not eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Hungriness is the state of wanting food, which is what an appetite means.

clue.text: Study O-Level Sociology essentially from the beginning

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence or heart of each word, so only its central letter is kept

blocks.note: a den is a private study room
taken as written
the central letter of level
the central letter of sociology

explanation.surface: Revising for a school sociology exam starting from scratch.
explanation.walkthrough: O-Level looks like one exam, but its O stands alone and Level and Sociology each give their middle letter. O-Levels were the old British school exams at sixteen.
explanation.definitionFit: De novo is a Latin phrase meaning anew, starting over afresh.

clue.text: Steep area – mind out!

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or wrong, telling us to rearrange the letters

blocks.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: A warning shout about a dangerously sloping patch of ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steep' looks like an adjective for a slope, but it is the verb for soaking food.
explanation.definitionFit: To marinade food is to soak it in a seasoned liquid, which is what steeping does.

clue.text: Liverpudlian exporting cocaine is 8

indicators.note: exporting sends goods out of the country, so a letter leaves the word

blocks.note: a Scouse is a native of Liverpool
C is slang for cocaine

explanation.surface: A man from Liverpool smuggling drugs out of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: SCOUSE loses its C. The definition is the answer to 8 across, MARINADE.
explanation.definitionFit: To souse food is to soak it in pickle or brine, the same as marinading it.

clue.text: Selection of soya beans on counter in marketplace

indicators.note: a selection is a part picked from a larger whole, so the letters sit inside the words
counter means running against the usual direction, so the letters are read right to left

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of soya and start of beans

explanation.surface: Soya beans laid out on a shop counter at a market.
explanation.definitionFit: eBay is a large online auction and trading website, a virtual marketplace.

clue.text: Grass in English garden mown regularly in well-to-do area

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: Kent is known as the Garden of England
to grass or sing is to inform on someone to the police
the second and fourth letters of mown

explanation.surface: Lawn in a neatly mowed garden in a posh district.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in south-east England nicknamed the Garden of England; 'Grass' looks like lawn but means to inform.
explanation.definitionFit: Kensington is an affluent district of west London, known for wealthy residents.

clue.text: Cold case for Detective Columbo finale is foolishness

indicators.note: a finale is the closing part, so only the last letter is used
a case holds its contents, so one piece wraps round the others

blocks.note: icy means very cold
DI is a Detective Inspector
the final letter of Columbo

explanation.surface: An unsolved crime in the last episode of a detective series is silly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold case' reads as an unsolved crime, but 'Cold' alone is the casing and 'case for' tells it to wrap the next pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiocy is extreme stupidity, behaviour or thinking that shows a lack of sense.

clue.text: Case dismissed by one dressed in leather?

indicators.note: being dressed in clothing means being wrapped inside it

blocks.note: a batter dismissed in cricket is out
the Roman numeral for one
patent leather is the glossy varnished kind

explanation.surface: A court case thrown out by a judge, or someone in leather gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case dismissed' sounds like a courtroom, but a case here is a medical patient.
explanation.definitionFit: An outpatient is a hospital case treated without staying overnight, and doctors call patients cases.

clue.text: Ford maybe failing to start in pursuit of German troops

indicators.note: failing to start means the beginning is missing, so the opening letter goes

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for German
the actor Harrison Ford; the 'maybe' marks him as one Ford of many

explanation.surface: An actor or a car breaking down while chasing German soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: HARRISON loses his H and follows G. 'Ford' suggests the car maker, but it is the actor's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A garrison is a body of soldiers stationed to defend a town or fort.

clue.text: Drink from unopened barrel

indicators.note: unopened suggests the opening is removed, so the first letter is lost

blocks.note: a drum is a cylindrical barrel

explanation.surface: Drawing a drink from a barrel that has not been tapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane, an alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Husband consumed by wrong ends in here?

indicators.note: something consumed is taken inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: to go astray is to go wrong
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A husband swallowed up by a wrong turn, ending up in some place.
explanation.walkthrough: H goes inside ASTRAY. The ends are cigarette ends, so the question mark flags a playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashtray is a dish where smokers stub out and leave their cigarette butts.

clue.text: Is that Bambi heading off for shelter?

indicators.note: with the heading gone, the first letter of the word is removed

blocks.note: Bambi is Disney's young deer, a fawn

explanation.surface: Wondering whether the cartoon deer is running off to hide.
explanation.walkthrough: FAWN loses its F. The definition is loose: an awn is the bristle on a grain such as barley, which guards the seed.
explanation.definitionFit: An awn is the stiff bristle growing from a grass flower, protecting the developing seed like a guard.

clue.text: Great blokes in semi-rough

indicators.note: rough means crude and unfinished, so the letters are roughed up into a new order
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
blokes is British slang for men

explanation.surface: Praise for some lads living in a run-down semi-detached house.
explanation.walkthrough: A semi is a British semi-detached house, one of a pair sharing a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Immense means huge or enormous, one sense of great in size.

clue.text: Cricketing legend Amiss sleeps it off

blocks.note: Sir Garfield Sobers, the great West Indies all-rounder
when something is amiss we ask what is up

explanation.surface: Dennis Amiss, an England batsman, resting after a night out.
explanation.walkthrough: Amiss looks like the surname of the England cricketer Dennis Amiss, but it means wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: To sober up is to recover from drunkenness, which sleeping it off achieves.

clue.text: Hassle travelling around India for Victorian women?

indicators.note: travelling letters are on the move, so they end up in another order
around means surrounding, so one piece is placed inside

blocks.note: taken as written
India is I in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Trouble on a journey through India for nineteenth-century ladies.
explanation.walkthrough: Victorian means from Victoria, the Australian state, not the era; the question mark flags the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheila is Australian slang for a woman, so Sheilas are women from Down Under.

clue.text: Animated studio producer's about to cover Virginia Plain

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the word is read backwards
covering something means going over and around it

blocks.note: William Hanna of the Hanna-Barbera cartoon studio, with the 's
VA is the postal abbreviation for Virginia

explanation.surface: A cartoon producer covering the Roxy Music song Virginia Plain.
explanation.walkthrough: Virginia Plain was a 1972 hit for Roxy Music, so the surface hides the definition in a song title.
explanation.definitionFit: A savannah is a flat grassy plain with scattered trees, typical of tropical Africa.

clue.text: Book is on time in the end

blocks.note: an atlas is a book of maps
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A library book returned on time after all.
explanation.definitionFit: At last means finally, after a long delay, the same as eventually.

clue.text: West Indies importing revolutionary fish paste

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so the word is read backwards
importing brings goods inside, so one piece is put within the other

blocks.note: WI is the standard abbreviation for West Indies
basa is a catfish from south-east Asia

explanation.surface: The Caribbean bringing in a radical new fish spread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish paste' looks like one item, but fish is wordplay and paste the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Wasabi is a pungent green Japanese condiment served as a paste with sushi.

clue.text: TV doctor eating a very large fish

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: Doctor Who, the long-running BBC science fiction series
taken as written
OS stands for outsize, a clothing size

explanation.surface: A television doctor tucking into a huge fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The wahoo is a fast predatory ocean fish related to the mackerel, prized for sport.

clue.text: Job in the chippie changes sides to make national dish of 1

indicators.note: changing sides means swapping right for left, so one letter is exchanged for its opposite

blocks.note: frying fish is the work done in a fish and chip shop

explanation.surface: A worker in a fish and chip shop switching to make a country's signature meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The R of FRYING FISH becomes L. A chippie is a British fish and chip shop; 1 is BARBADOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Flying fish served with cou-cou is the recognised national dish of the Caribbean island.

clue.text: Breaks wind quietly inside

indicators.note: inside places the letter within the other word

blocks.note: gas is wind in the digestive sense
p is the musical marking piano, quietly

explanation.surface: Someone discreetly passing wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaks wind' looks like one phrase, but Breaks is the definition and wind the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaps are intervals or pauses, the same as breaks in an activity.

clue.text: Cool retro case for AirPods

indicators.note: retro means backward-looking, so the letters are read in reverse
a case is the outside, so only the outer letters of the word are kept

blocks.note: cool as in fine or acceptable
the first and last letters of air

explanation.surface: A trendy old-style case for wireless earphones.
explanation.walkthrough: AirPods splits in two: Air gives the outer letters, which are reversed to RA, and Pods is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Okra is a vegetable consisting of the long green seed pods of a mallow plant.

clue.text: Serving of Navratilova lost shape

indicators.note: a serving is a portion of something larger, so the letters are a part of the words

blocks.note: the end of Navratilova and start of lost

explanation.surface: Martina Navratilova losing her serve in a tennis match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serving' and 'lost' sound like tennis, but serving is the indicator; Navratilova was a champion tennis player.
explanation.definitionFit: An oval is an elongated rounded figure like an egg outline, a geometric form.

clue.text: Dawn French for one tucked into drink

indicators.note: tucked into means placed snugly inside

blocks.note: to sup is to drink
un is French for one

explanation.surface: The comedian Dawn French having a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Dawn French is a British comic actor, so the surface glues the definition onto her surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunup is the moment of sunrise, the start of the day, which is dawn.

clue.text: Stomach's a problem after lamb korma occasionally

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is kept
after says the earlier clue words are placed second, following the later ones

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters
taken as written
a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: Indigestion after eating a lamb curry.
explanation.walkthrough: The lamb is apt: the abomasum is the fourth stomach of a ruminant such as a sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: The abomasum is the fourth chamber of a cow's or sheep's digestive system, its true digestive organ.
